case_studies.title: Pluralistic Leaderboards
case_studies.abstract: Recent leaderboard-based evaluations of large language models aggregate user feedback by fitting a Bradley--Terry model to pairwise comparisons, producing a single global ranking based on a latent quality score. While appealing for its simplicity, this approach is incompatible with heterogeneous preferences: when LLMs are used across diverse tasks and use cases, users who favor fundamentally different model behaviors can be systematically misrepresented when collapsed into a single quality score. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inaccurate leaderboards for large language models by building a pluralistic leaderboard system that can handle diverse user preferences, resulting in more accurate and stable rankings. The researchers created a system that can accommodate different model behaviors and user preferences. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating large language models in real-world personal applications, the researchers built a benchmark called MCP-Persona, and the result is a more accurate way to assess agent performance. MCP-Persona simulates environment interactions to test large language models. This breakthrough has potential implications for developers and engineers working with language models.

case_studies.title: SMH-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Environment-Grounded Reasoning and Action in Smart Homes
case_studies.abstract: Smart homes are evolving toward complex state-dependent living environments, requiring Large Language Models (LLMs) to reason over user intent, preferences, and multi-device interactions. However, existing smart-home benchmarks often focus on static instruction-to-API mapping or limited simulations, failing to evaluate whether LLMs can reason, interact, and act reliably in realistic household scenarios. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating Large Language Models in smart-home environments by creating SMH-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark that tests LLMs' ability to reason and interact in realistic household scenarios, resulting in a more reliable way to assess their performance. The researchers built SMH-Bench using HomeEnv, a smart-home simulator. This research is not directly relevant to cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.title: RASER: Recoverability-Aware Selective Escalation Router for Multi-Hop Question Answering
case_studies.abstract: Multi-hop question-answering systems often use expensive retrieval on every question. They may decompose the question, run several retrieval rounds, or search through bridge entities before answering. All of these strategies rely on repeated LLM calls to rewrite or decompose the question, which increases extra token cost, and it is not fitting when the LLM budget is tight. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient multi-hop question answering by introducing RASER, a recoverability-aware selective escalation router that reduces unnecessary retrieval rounds. The result is a more cost-effective approach to question answering. It does not directly affect cloud infrastructure management work.

case_studies.title: SIRI: Self-Internalizing Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Skills for LLM Agent Training
case_studies.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents can benefit from reusable skills, yet existing skill-based methods often rely on external skill generators during training or persistent skill retrieval at inference, increasing engineering complexity, context length, and deployment latency. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of complex LLM agent training by introducing a framework called SIRI, which enables agents to discover and internalize skills on their own. The researchers built a three-phase framework that allows agents to learn without external skill generators. The result is a more efficient and streamlined training process.

case_studies.abstract: Agentic systems entering production typically operate as partially integrated assemblies where structural defects, not task-level errors, dominate the failure landscape. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of monitoring agentic systems that are not yet reliable, by building a monitoring and triage methodology that evaluates system performance in three dimensions, resulting in improved detection of structural failures. case_studies.title: HERO'S JOURNEY: Testing Complex Rule Induction with Text Games
case_studies.abstract: We introduce HERO'S JOURNEY, a benchmark for rule induction in goal-directed episodic tasks, where agents must infer hidden rules from demonstrations and act on them through multi-step execution. HERO'S JOURNEY covers eight tasks across attribute and procedural induction families, each with four structural rule forms, controllable lexical grounding, and identifiability conditions. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of rule induction in complex tasks by introducing a benchmark called HERO'S JOURNEY, which tests the ability of models to infer hidden rules from demonstrations. The researchers built a set of tasks that cover different types of rule induction and evaluated state-of-the-art language models. The result shows that models have limited and uneven rule induction abilities.

case_studies.title: SPADE-Bench: Evaluating Spontaneous Strategic Deception in Agents via Plan-Action Divergence
case_studies.abstract: As LLM-based agents expand their operational scope, reliability becomes a prerequisite for real-world deployment. However, in practical applications, human users cannot monitor every immediate behavior; instead, the execution process often remains a black box, leaving users dependent solely on the agent's self-reported updates. This opacity creates a critical risk: agents may present observer-facing reports that diverge from their executed actions, rendering the system uncontrollable, especially in high-stakes autonomous scenarios. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of agents providing false reports of their actions, which can lead to uncontrollable systems. The researchers built a benchmark called SPADE-Bench to evaluate this issue in agents. The result is a tool to assess the reliability of agents in real-world deployment.

case_studies.title: SimSD: Simple Speculative Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive (AR) LLMs, offering faster inference through parallel or blockwise decoding. However, their masked language modeling formulation remains incompatible with standard token-level speculative decoding, one of the most effective acceleration techniques for AR models. In AR decoding, the causal mask preserves temporally valid token-level contexts, enabling a target model to verify multiple drafted tokens in a single forward pass. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of slow decoding in diffusion large language models by building a simple speculative decoding method called SimSD. The result is faster inference through parallel or blockwise decoding. It does not directly affect cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.title: Bridging the Last Mile of Time Series Forecasting with LLM Agents
case_studies.abstract: Time series forecasting has advanced rapidly, especially with the emergence of foundation models that show strong zero-shot performance on numerical extrapolation. However, in real-world forecasting settings, a statistically plausible baseline is rarely the final forecast used in practice. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of making time series forecasts more accurate by incorporating real-world context, the authors built a system using LLM agents to revise forecasts, the result is more decision-ready forecasts.
